TRILLION PESO MARCH ORGANIZERS SEAL COMMITMENT FOR PEACEFUL ASSEMBLY ON SEPTEMBER 21

Organizers of the upcoming Trillion Peso March have signed a Memorandum of Undertaking affirming their commitment to a peaceful and orderly assembly on September 21 at the People Power Monument.

The agreement was signed by the Church Leaders Council for National Transformation (CLCNT), Simbahan at Komunidad Laban sa Katiwalian (SIKLAB), Alyansa ng Nagkakaisang Mamamayan (ANIM), Taumbayan Ayaw sa Magnanakaw at Abusado Network Alliance (TAMA NA), the Quezon City Police District (QCPD), and Tindig Pilipinas.

The program will begin with an ecumenical mass and morning program led by SIKLAB at 9:00 AM, followed by the main protest action in the afternoon, also at the People Power Monument. The public is invited to participate.

"The Trillion Peso March is not just a protest—it is a moral call. On September 21, we show that the people will not be silenced by corruption and abuse. Together, we march in peace, but with firm conviction, to demand a government worthy of our trust," said Kiko Aquino Dee of Tindig Pilipinas.

Organizers urged Filipinos nationwide to join the march.

"September 21 will be a day to show that when the people stand together—peacefully but resolutely—no abuse of power can outlast the strength of a nation determined to reclaim integrity in governance," Dee added.

FOUR PROTEST VENUES IN METRO MANILA FOR SEPT 21–WHERE ARE YOU HEADED? 

LUNETA - headed and organized by rappers and hip hop artists

EDSA -  organized by Kiko Aquino Dee and the Makabayan Bloc (YELLOWS and REDS) 

LIWASAN BONIFACIO - organized by MAISUG 
(VIC RODRIGUEZ, etc) 

CAMP AGUINALDO - organized by retired military

Despite the many venues for rallies this Sept 21, dalawang klase ng rally lang talaga ang meron, ideologically speaking. 

Yung isa, para managot ang President (as a matter of command responsibility) at ang mga Congressmen and everyone involved in the blatant corruption. 

Hindi lang sa Flood Control Project, kasama na rin ang Philhealth, gold selling, Maharlika Funds. 

So it has a clear clarion call, they will tell
you in no uncertain terms of the end or goal they want to achieve. May definite goal ang rallies nila— a change in leadership. 

Yung isa naman, they’re clarifying na their rallies is not to ask BBM to resign. They’re saying that it’s an anti corruption rally. 

No asking anybody to resign. But  im not sure if an anti corruption rally is necessary without any call to action, because is there a pro corruption rally they’re fighting against? 

What is the clamor in certain terms?  Who are they going to ask for answers? Or is this a prayer rally? 

Confused ako sa call to action ng other rally.

Anyway, It’s going to an interesting Sept 21 here in Manila. 

Meanwhile, in Davao, Cagayan, and Bacolod there will be rallies as well. If you’re from these places please check where yours might be.

Source: Kiffy Chu 
https://t.co/cl6nysQ1Zu
